info.title: SP Trading API
info.description:
Machine interface of SP Wallet: market data, portfolio, positions, orders, strategies and agents.

Human-readable reference, generated from this document and served by the same server: `GET /api/v1/trading/docs` (HTML: getting started, concepts, one section per operation, the error catalogue) and `GET /api/v1/trading/docs.md` (the same as Markdown). Those two paths and the websocket below are the only paths under the prefix that are not operations of this document.

Every operation carries a worked example: the request (`example` on parameters and on the request body), the 200 answer (`example` on the response; `x-spw-example-recorded: true` when it is a real recorded answer), and the same call as curl, TypeScript and Python (`x-codeSamples`; `client` is an `SPWallet` of the SDK, built from the environment variables `SP_WALLET_API_KEY` and `SP_WALLET_BASE_URL`).

What each error code means and what to do about it: `x-spw-error-catalog` (every code of every `x-spw-errors`). The reasons of a `mandate_denied`: `x-spw-mandate-deny-reason-docs`. The twelve order states: `x-spw-order-states`, each explained in `x-spw-order-state-docs`; the scopes in `x-spw-scope-docs`.

Live trading with a key exists on Hyperliquid only (the perpetuals of its own dex, ids `hyperliquid:BTC`); GMX orders are the owner's, approved in the app; dYdX and edgeX are market data only. Paper orders are simulated by the wallet against the real Hyperliquid order book.

Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer spw_live_…` (an API key created by the owner with his passkey). A key opens nothing outside `/api/v1/trading/`.

Every operation names the scope it needs (`x-spw-scope`). Scopes are access control inside the API; they are not what bounds execution: an order placed with a key is bounded by a trading mandate that the isolated signer enforces, and execution scopes are inert without one.

Numbers that carry money are decimal strings. Paper and live data always carry a `mode` and are never merged.

Errors are `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<sentence>" }`, with `data` when a refusal has machine-readable detail (the order it is about, the mandate's reasons, the failed risk checks, the questions of an ambiguous command). Every operation lists the codes it can answer, with their status, in `x-spw-errors`. A 400 `bad_request` produced by input validation also carries `data.fields`: one `{ path, code, message }` per refused member (what is expected, never the value that was sent). Rate limits are per key: `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds).

A path that is not an operation of this document (or a known path with another method) answers 404 `not_found` in the same error model.

Live market data (quotes, order books, trades, candles, venue statuses) is also served over a websocket, which this document cannot describe: `GET /api/v1/trading/stream` (scope `markets:read`; the key in the `Authorization` header of the handshake, or `?ticket=` with a single-use ticket from `POST /api/v1/trading/stream/ticket`). See `docs/V11-QUOTE-ENGINE.md`. A stream connection writes no row in the key's usage log — it is counted in the stream's own statistics; the ticket request is an ordinary call and is logged like any other.

An order's `status` is one of the twelve states of `x-spw-order-states`; `final` is true for the states marked final. `UNKNOWN` is neither final nor a failure. Lists that can grow without bound (`GET /orders`, `GET /activity`) are paginated with `cursor` / `nextCursor`.

tags.name: Markets
tags.description: Public market data: instruments across venues, tickers, order books, candles, the venue comparator, and the synthetic contracts on private companies. Scope `markets:read`. Reading a venue does not mean it can be traded: live orders with a key exist on Hyperliquid only.

tags.name: Portfolio
tags.description: What the wallet holds: on-chain balances, the valued portfolio with every derivatives account, and the activity feed. Scope `wallet:read`. Paper and live are separate figures, never summed.

tags.name: Nfts
tags.description: Read-only NFT data: the wallet's inventory (`wallet:read`) and market data of any item (`markets:read`). No transfer and no market write exists in this API. An NFT never has a value here.

tags.name: Positions
tags.description: Open positions, and the two ways out of one: close and reduce — strictly reduce-only market orders. Closing passes the kill switch.

tags.name: Orders
tags.description: Preview, place, read and cancel orders, and the one-line command grammar. Every order passes the key, the mandate, the risk engine and the venue engine, in that order; a refusal names its gate.

tags.name: Strategies
tags.description: The strategy library and the versions pinned to agents: register, backtest, start, stop. Research and paper sign nothing.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Trading agents: templates, lifecycle (create, start, pause, stop), and their history read ONE mode per call (research, paper or live). An agent goes live only under its own owner-approved mandate.

tags.name: Risk
tags.description: The state of the risk engine and of the server locks, and the one control a key has: engaging the global kill switch (never releasing it).

get.summary: Compare the estimated cost of one position across venues
get.description: One row per venue for a common underlying, from the real instrument, order book (GMX: pool figures), ticker, fee schedule and funding rate read now: spread, depth within 10/25/50 bps, slippage for the notional, fees, funding expected over the horizon (current rate held constant), collateral, liquidation estimate and the itemised total. Every figure is an estimate; a missing input gives null with its reason. Venues the wallet cannot trade on are shown and flagged. `discrepancies` are estimates with their assumptions and risks, never a recommendation.

Idempotent on (principal, Idempotency-Key): a replay answers the same order and never sends a second request to a venue; the same key with a different order answers 409 `idempotency_conflict`.

Owner session: the order is checked and waits `AWAITING_APPROVAL` until the owner approves it with the passkey in the app (paper: executed at once, nothing is signed).

API key: needs a trading mandate bound to the key that covers the order exactly (403 `mandate_denied` with the reasons otherwise), then the risk engine, then the venue engine's mandate path — the isolated signer applies the derivative mandate it stores.

LIVE needs `SPW_TRADING_API_EXECUTION=on` on the server (403 `execution_disabled` otherwise) and the existing mainnet locks. Live orders with a key exist on Hyperliquid only.

A refusal after the order exists answers 4xx with the order in `data.order` (state `REJECTED` or `FAILED`). An outcome that is not known is `UNKNOWN`, never a failure.

Spot orders: 403 `spot_execution_requires_agent_vault` for a key; 422 `spot_via_swap_screen` for the owner. The venue engine that executes the order can refuse it with a code of its own rules that this list does not name (`x-spw-errors-open`): the HTTP status still tells the class, and the order is in `data.order`.
post.x-spw-example-note: A paper market order is filled at once by the paper engine against the real Hyperliquid book: `status` is already `FILLED`.

post.summary: Run one line of the trading command grammar
post.description:
Deterministic grammar (no model): LONG|SHORT <asset>-PERP <notional> [x<lev>] [LIMIT <px>] [SL <px>] [TP <px>] [ON <venue>], CLOSE <asset>-PERP [pct%], CANCEL ORDER <id>, CANCEL ALL, SHOW POSITIONS|BALANCES|ORDERS|RISK, STOP ALL AGENTS, KILL, and for the owner BUY/SELL (spot).

The scope checked is the one of the operation the command resolves to: an order needs `orders:execute` (`orders:prepare` with `dryRun`), CLOSE `positions:manage`, CANCEL `orders:cancel`, SHOW the matching read scope, KILL `positions:manage`.

Resolution uses the owner's stored defaults (GET/PUT /api/v1/developer/command-defaults) and nothing else: a command the defaults do not settle answers 409 `ambiguous_command` with the questions in `data.questions` and executes nothing.

`kind` says what the command resolved to: `query` (the read answer is in `data`), `control` (a cancel or the kill switch) or `order`. A spot order (BUY ETH 100 USDC, SELL ETH 0.5) is the owner's: it becomes a swap proposal approved with the passkey. The venue engine that executes the order can refuse it with a code of its own rules that this list does not name (`x-spw-errors-open`): the HTTP status still tells the class, and the order is in `data.order`.
post.x-spw-example-note: A dry run: the canonical order the line resolves to, and nothing created. Needs the owner's command defaults (see Commands).

bad_state.meaning: The object is not in a state that allows this: an order being handed to its engine right now, a swap already approved, an agent or job already in that state.
bad_state.action: Read the object again; for an order, ask again in a moment.

bad_strategy.meaning: The laboratory refused the strategy file.

duplicate_client_id.action: Use a new `clientOrderId` / Idempotency-Key for a new order.

execution_disabled.meaning: Live execution through the trading API is closed on this server (`SPW_TRADING_API_EXECUTION` is not `on`). Nothing was created.
execution_disabled.action: Paper is not affected; cancels and strictly reducing orders still pass. The server operator opens the lock.

execution_not_wired.meaning: The operation exists in the contract and is not connected on this server (or, for STOP ALL AGENTS, could stop nothing from here). Never a success: nothing was done.
execution_not_wired.action: Do not retry. Use the operation the message points to.

fee_cap_not_expressible.meaning: The quote asset is not one the owner's defaults count as USD, so the fee cap cannot be expressed.
fee_cap_not_expressible.action: Use a USD quote, or the owner adds it to the defaults (`usdQuotes`).

gmx_disabled.meaning: GMX live trading is switched off (server lock or owner setting).
gmx_disabled.action: Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

gmx_leverage_required.meaning: A GMX increase must name its `leverage` (GMX has no leverage setting to fall back on).

gmx_requires_owner_passkey.meaning: Every GMX order is a wallet transaction the owner approves with the passkey: a key or an agent cannot place, close or cancel one.

gross_exposure_exceeded.meaning: The resulting gross exposure exceeds the account policy.
gross_exposure_exceeded.action: Reduce first, or send a smaller order.

halted.meaning: 423/422: the signer's emergency halt is active, or the account is halted. 409 (agents): the agent's paper account is halted.
halted.action: Cancels and reduce-only exits are still signed. The halt is lifted on the signer machine only.

idempotency.meaning: A mutating call without a valid `Idempotency-Key` header (8 to 100 characters: letters, digits, `.` `_` `:` `-`).
idempotency.action: Send the header. One key per logical action; keep it for retries.

idempotency_conflict.meaning: This Idempotency-Key (or `clientOrderId`) was already used with a DIFFERENT request, or belongs to another principal.
idempotency_conflict.action: A new action needs a new key. To retry the first action, send the first request again, byte for byte.

idempotency_in_progress.meaning: The first call with this Idempotency-Key is still running, or just ended without an answer.
idempotency_in_progress.action: Wait a second and send the same call again.

inconsistent_prices.meaning: The stop-loss / take-profit are on the wrong side of the entry or of each other.
inconsistent_prices.action: A long: SL below entry, TP above. A short: the reverse.

instrument_halted.meaning: The venue has halted this instrument.
instrument_halted.action: Nothing to do until the venue reopens it.

instrument_mismatch.meaning: The account is on one venue and the instrument on another.
instrument_mismatch.action: Name the account of the instrument's venue.

instrument_not_allowed.meaning: The instrument is not allowed by the account's authorization or policy.
instrument_not_allowed.action: Trade an allowed instrument, or the owner widens the policy.

instrument_reduce_only.meaning: The venue only accepts orders that reduce a position on this instrument.

insufficient_collateral.meaning: Not enough free collateral on the account for this order.
insufficient_collateral.action: Send a smaller order, or the owner adds collateral to the account.

insufficient_scope.meaning: The key does not hold the permission (scope) this operation needs. For POST /commands: the scope of the operation the command resolves to.
insufficient_scope.action: Use a key that holds the scope named in `message`. Adding a scope to a key needs the owner's passkey.

internal.meaning: The server failed. A mutating call may or may not have run.
internal.action: Send the same call again with the SAME Idempotency-Key: it either returns the stored answer or runs once. Do not create a new key for a retry.

invalid_cursor.meaning: The `cursor` is not one a previous page of this list returned.
invalid_cursor.action: Start again without a cursor; send a cursor with the same filters it came with.

invalid_order.meaning: The order is not well-formed for its type: a limit without `price`, a stop without `triggerPrice`, `reduceOnly` on spot, a research-mode order, a mandate or principal that is not the caller's.
invalid_order.action: Fix the request; sending it again unchanged gives the same answer.

ip_not_allowed.meaning: The key has an IP allow-list and the request came from another address.
ip_not_allowed.action: Call from an allowed address, or have the owner change the key's restrictions.

key_limit_exceeded.meaning: The order is above the key's own notional limit (per order or per day), or cannot be valued so the limit cannot be checked.
key_limit_exceeded.action: Send a smaller order; the limits are on the key (Developer → Keys).

kill_switch_active.meaning: The global kill switch is on: no new risk for anybody, on any venue, in any mode.
kill_switch_active.action: Cancels and strictly reducing orders still pass. Only the owner releases it, with the passkey.

leverage_exceeded.meaning: The leverage is above the authorized maximum (policy, mandate or venue).

leverage_mismatch.meaning: A live order names a leverage that is not the venue's current setting for the instrument.
leverage_mismatch.action: Send the order without `leverage`, or the owner changes the setting in the app.

liquidation_too_close.meaning: The estimated liquidation price after the order is closer to the mark than the policy allows.

live_not_available.meaning: A paper account can only be PAPER or READ_ONLY.
live_not_available.action: Use a venue account for live.

live_unavailable.meaning: This agent family cannot go live (the message says why).

mainnet_disabled.meaning: The server lock for new mainnet risk is closed (`SPW_DERIV_LIVE_MAINNET`).
mainnet_disabled.action: Paper works; cancels and reductions pass. Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

mandate_denied.meaning: The order is outside the mandate. `data.reasons` lists EVERY reason (codes of the mandate table, e.g. `ORDER_NOTIONAL_EXCEEDED`, `INSTRUMENT_NOT_ALLOWED`); `data.order` is the order, state REJECTED.
mandate_denied.action: Change the order to fit the mandate; a wider mandate is a new mandate approved by the owner.

mandate_integrity.meaning: The stored mandate no longer hashes to what the owner's passkey approved. It is unusable and gets revoked.
mandate_integrity.action: The owner approves a new mandate.

mandate_mainnet_disabled.meaning: The server lock for mandates on mainnet is closed (`SPW_DERIV_MANDATE_MAINNET`).
mandate_mainnet_disabled.action: Paper works; cancels and reductions pass. Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

mandate_mismatch.meaning: The mandate was approved for another strategy version or another agent.
mandate_mismatch.action: The owner approves a mandate for this one.

mandate_none.meaning: Live: no derivative mandate is in force at the signer for this venue account.
mandate_none.action: The owner approves a live mandate with the passkey.

mandate_not_approved.meaning: The mandate bound to this principal was never approved, or is no longer active.
mandate_not_approved.action: The owner approves a mandate and binds it.

mandate_required.meaning: 403: an execution scope is inert on this key because no trading mandate is bound to it. 409 (agents): going live needs a mandate the owner approved for that agent.
mandate_required.action: The owner creates and approves a mandate for the key (Settings → Risk → Trading mandates), then binds it to the key. See Mandates.

mandate_unavailable.meaning: Live mandates are not available on this server (a server lock).
mandate_unavailable.action: Paper works. Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

mandate_wind_down.meaning: The mandate was revoked or has expired: for 24 h only cancels and reduce-only orders are placed.
mandate_wind_down.action: Reduce or close; new risk needs a new mandate.

mark_index_divergence.meaning: Mark and index prices are further apart than the policy allows.

markets_unavailable.meaning: No market source at all could be read.
markets_unavailable.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

missing_balance.meaning: A percentage of a balance was asked and the balance could not be read.
missing_balance.action: Retry, or name an absolute quantity.

missing_reference_price.meaning: No USD reference price is available to express the fee cap.
missing_reference_price.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

mixed_credentials.meaning: The request carried an API key and a session cookie (or a stream ticket) together.
mixed_credentials.action: Send exactly one credential. A script never sends the cookie.

mode_read_only.meaning: The venue account is read-only: live trading was never authorized with the owner's passkey, or the authorization was revoked.
mode_read_only.action: The owner authorizes the account in Futures → Accounts.

nft_bad_identifier.meaning: The address or token id is not well-formed for the network.
nft_bad_identifier.action: Fix the request; sending it again unchanged gives the same answer.

nft_budget_exhausted.meaning: The wallet's own request budget for a metered provider is spent for now.

nft_disabled.meaning: The NFT module is switched off on this server.

nft_not_found.meaning: The chain does not know this item.
nft_not_found.action: Check network, address and token id.

nft_provider_bad_answer.meaning: A provider answered something that could not be interpreted.
nft_provider_bad_answer.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

nft_provider_disagreement.meaning: Sources disagree on a fact the answer needs.
nft_provider_disagreement.action: Read GET /nfts/market: each source is on its own row.

nft_provider_method_unsupported.meaning: The provider cannot answer this kind of question for this network.

nft_provider_not_configured.meaning: The provider this call needs has no key on the server.
nft_provider_not_configured.action: The answer names the server variable; the operator sets it.

nft_provider_rate_limited.meaning: A market-data provider is rate-limiting this wallet.
nft_provider_rate_limited.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

nft_provider_unavailable.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

nft_unsupported_chain.meaning: No NFT adapter for this network.
nft_unsupported_chain.action: Use Solana or one of the EVM networks.

nft_unsupported_standard.meaning: The contract is not an NFT standard this wallet reads.

no_account.meaning: No paper account (mode `paper`) or no authorized venue account (mode `live`) on this venue.
no_account.action: The owner creates a paper account, or authorizes a venue account with the passkey, in Futures → Accounts.

no_client_id_format.meaning: The venue has no client-order-id format this wallet can derive.
no_client_id_format.action: Use a venue the wallet trades.

no_instrument.meaning: The command names an asset no instrument of the catalogue matches (on that venue/network).
no_instrument.action: Check the asset and the venue.

no_liquidity.meaning: The book has no bid/ask from which to derive a price for a market order.
no_liquidity.action: Retry later, or send a limit order.

no_orderbook.meaning: The venue has no order book (GMX is a liquidity pool; spot market data stores bars).

no_position.meaning: There is no open position to close or reduce on that instrument and account.

no_report.meaning: The strategy version has no backtest report.
no_report.action: Run POST /strategies/{id}/backtest and wait for the job.

no_strategy.meaning: The agent has no approved strategy version.
no_strategy.action: Register one with POST /strategies and let its backtest finish.

not_a_private_market.meaning: The instrument exists and is not a private-company contract.

not_found.meaning: Agents: no such agent, strategy version or job (or the key is restricted away from it). Any other path: not an operation of this API.
not_found.action: Check the id; list with GET /agents or GET /strategies. For a path, see the operation list.

not_reducing.meaning: The order would not strictly reduce an existing position: nothing was placed.
not_reducing.action: Read GET /positions; the position may already be closed.

not_your_order.meaning: A key cancels its own orders only.
not_your_order.action: The owner cancels anything, in the app.

order_notional_exceeded.meaning: The order is above the account policy's notional per order.

order_rate_day.meaning: Too many orders on this account today (account policy).
order_rate_day.action: Wait for the next day; Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

order_rate_minute.meaning: Too many orders on this account in the last minute (account policy).

other_version.meaning: Only the most recent version of an agent can be started (or: the agent runs another approved version).
other_version.action: Register the version again, or start the current one.

owner_required.meaning: Only the owner can do this: create a spot agent (its vault is derived by the signer), let the supervisor act on live agents.

owner_session_required.meaning: A spot order (a swap proposal) is prepared and withdrawn in the owner's session, not with a key.

paper_unsupported.meaning: The venue has no order book, so the paper engine cannot fill against it (GMX).

parse_error.meaning: The text is not a sentence of the command grammar. `data.code` is the grammar's own code and `data.token` the index of the offending token.
parse_error.action: Fix the line; the grammar is in the Commands section.

position_not_attributable.meaning: A key or an agent closes only the part of a position its own fills opened; this position (or that share of it) was opened by the owner or another principal.
position_not_attributable.action: Close only what the key opened; the owner closes anything.

position_notional_exceeded.meaning: The resulting position exceeds the account policy for the instrument.

price_deviation.meaning: The price is further from the mark (or the trigger) than the account policy allows (`maxDeviationBps`; GET /risk shows the policy of each account).
price_deviation.action: Price the order closer to the mark. The mark is in GET /markets/{symbol}.

price_not_on_tick.meaning: The price is not a multiple of the instrument's `tickSize` (or has too many decimals for the venue).
price_not_on_tick.action: Round the price to `tickSize` — as a decimal STRING, not a float.

price_required.meaning: A limit order needs `price` (a market order needs a worst acceptable price, which the server derives).

rate_limited.meaning: More calls than the key's per-minute limit in the current one-minute window.
rate_limited.action: Wait `Retry-After` seconds (also `RateLimit-Reset`), then go on. Both SDKs do this for you.

read_only_mode.meaning: Read-only mode is on: only cancels pass (or: an agent in research mode places no order).
read_only_mode.action: Cancel if needed; the owner releases it with the passkey.

reduce_only_would_flip.meaning: A reduce-only order is larger than the position.
reduce_only_would_flip.action: Size it at most to the position; POST /positions/{id}/close does it for you.

reduce_only_would_increase.meaning: A reduce-only order would open or increase a position.
reduce_only_would_increase.action: Check the side and the position.

restricted.meaning: The key's restrictions (venues, instruments, networks) exclude what the call names.
restricted.action: Use a venue, instrument or network the key is allowed on, or have the owner widen the key (passkey).

risk_denied.meaning: The independent risk engine refused the order. `data.failed` lists the failed check ids and `data.checks` gives, for each, what was observed and the limit; `data.order` is the order, state REJECTED.
risk_denied.action: Read `data.checks`. Frequent: a limit never configured on the live book, stale prices, an order too large for the collateral. See the risk checks table.

service_unavailable.meaning: No network / no position source could be read.
service_unavailable.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

signer_unreachable.meaning: The isolated signer cannot be reached: balances, the portfolio and anything that needs a signature are unavailable.
signer_unreachable.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key. If it lasts, the owner checks the signer machine.

size_not_on_lot.meaning: The size is not a multiple of `lotSize`.
size_not_on_lot.action: Round the size down to `lotSize`, or send `notional` and let the server size it.

spot_buy_needs_quote_amount.meaning: A swap is exact-input: a spot BUY names the amount of the quote asset to spend.
spot_buy_needs_quote_amount.action: Send `notional` (not `size`) for a spot buy, or the command `BUY ETH 100 USDC`.

spot_execution_requires_agent_vault.meaning: An API key cannot place a spot order: spot execution for keys and agents exists only through an agent vault under a spot mandate.
spot_execution_requires_agent_vault.action: Trade perpetuals with the key, or let a spot agent do it.

spot_market_only.meaning: A spot order here is an immediate swap bounded by `slippageBps`: resting and trigger orders do not exist for spot.

spot_paper_not_available.meaning: There is no paper spot engine for the owner.
spot_paper_not_available.action: Use mode `live` (a real swap, approved with the passkey); paper spot exists for agents only.

spot_via_swap_screen.meaning: An owner's spot order is a swap proposal approved with the passkey.
spot_via_swap_screen.action: Prepare it in the Swap screen.

stale_book.meaning: The order book is older than the account policy allows.

stale_data.meaning: The price or book needed is older than its freshness bound (e.g. a notional cannot be turned into a size at a stale mark).
stale_data.action: Retry in a few seconds. A limit order sized with `size` names its own price and does not depend on the mark.

stale_request.meaning: `X-SPW-Timestamp` was sent and is more than 300 s from the server clock (or is not Unix seconds).
stale_request.action: Fix the client clock, or do not send the header: it is optional.

stale_ticker.meaning: The venue ticker is older than the account policy allows (`maxDataAgeMs`).

strategy_not_installed.meaning: No strategy of this template is installed in the laboratory. Nothing was created (no placeholder is substituted).

swap_flow_failed.meaning: The swap flow returned no proposal.
swap_flow_failed.action: Retry; if it lasts, prepare the swap in the app to see the reason.

swap_not_enabled.meaning: The wallet does not execute swaps on this network.
swap_not_enabled.action: Use a network where swaps are enabled.

total_loss_exceeded.meaning: The account's total loss limit is reached.
total_loss_exceeded.action: Reductions pass; Only the owner can change this, in the app, with the passkey.

trigger_required.meaning: A stop or take-profit order needs `triggerPrice`.

unauthenticated.meaning: No credential, or a key that is malformed, unknown, wrong, expired or revoked. One answer for all of them, on purpose.
unauthenticated.action: Check the `Authorization: Bearer spw_live_…` header and the key's status and expiry in Developer → Keys. Ten failures a minute from one address lead to `auth_throttled`.

universe_mismatch.meaning: A fixed-universe strategy runs on its exact universe; the agent's differs.
universe_mismatch.action: Create the agent with the universe the message lists.

unknown_account.meaning: No paper account / authorized venue account with this `accountId` on the venue.
unknown_account.action: Omit `accountId` when the wallet has one account on the venue; else take it from GET /portfolio (`accounts`).

unknown_company.meaning: No reviewed private-company contract under this slug.

unknown_instrument.meaning: 404: the venue does not list this instrument. 422: an instrument the order path cannot use (not in the pinned table of the venue). 503: the venue could not be read to find out.
unknown_instrument.action: Take ids from GET /markets (`venue:symbol`). On 503 retry later.

unknown_market.meaning: A spot symbol without data, or a bare symbol nothing answers to.

unknown_network.meaning: The network id is not one of the wallet's.

unknown_nft.meaning: This NFT is not in the wallet's inventory.
unknown_nft.action: Take `key` from GET /nfts. For any other item use GET /nfts/market.

unknown_order.meaning: No order with this id (or none this key may see).
unknown_order.action: Take ids from GET /orders or from the answer of POST /orders.

unknown_position.meaning: The position id is not of the form GET /positions returns, or names nothing.
unknown_position.action: Take `id` from GET /positions and URL-encode it.

unknown_private_market.meaning: This id is not a private-company market known to the venues the wallet reads.

unknown_underlying.meaning: No perpetual is mapped to this underlying in the comparator.
unknown_underlying.action: Use an underlying that GET /markets lists as a `base`.

unknown_venue.meaning: The venue id is not one this wallet knows (`hyperliquid`, `gmx`, `dydx`, `edgex`, `spot`).

unsupported_asset.meaning: The base or quote asset is not exactly one asset of the wallet registry on that network.
unsupported_asset.action: Name assets the wallet lists in GET /balances.

unsupported_interval.meaning: Spot market data does not store this candle interval.
unsupported_interval.action: Use one of the intervals the message lists.

venue_not_wired.meaning: Live orders on this venue are not placed through this endpoint (GMX: prepared in the app, one passkey per order). This endpoint places live orders on Hyperliquid only.
venue_not_wired.action: Use `hyperliquid:*` for live orders through the API.

venue_rate_limited.meaning: The venue is rate-limiting this wallet.
venue_rate_limited.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

venue_rejected.meaning: The venue itself refused (the message quotes it): the order, a cancel, a margin mode it does not offer.

venue_restricted.meaning: The venue is never tradable from this wallet (dYdX and edgeX: market data only, a jurisdiction restriction).
venue_restricted.action: Read its data; trade on Hyperliquid.

venue_timeout.meaning: The venue did not answer in time and no earlier value can stand in.
venue_timeout.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

venue_unavailable.meaning: The venue (or the signer, for the wallet address) could not be read, so no honest answer exists.
venue_unavailable.action: Nothing was done. Retry with backoff; a mutating call keeps the same Idempotency-Key.

wrong_kind.meaning: The strategy and the agent are of different kinds (spot / perp), or the operation does not apply to this kind of agent.

x-spw-webhook-events.description: an API key was revoked (or replaced by a rotation)
the emergency halt of the signer was triggered (source "signer"), or the global kill switch of the risk engine was engaged or released (source "risk_engine")
x-spw-webhook-events.payload: { source: "signer", halted: true } | { source: "risk_engine", engaged, by, reason }

x-spw-webhook-events.description: an agent was started, paused or stopped (by the owner, an API key or the risk-management agent)
the risk-management agent proposes a reduction or a pause, or acted (paused an agent, engaged the kill switch)
x-spw-webhook-events.payload: { supervisorId, agentId, mode, action, code, acted, message, metrics }

x-spw-webhook-events.description: an order changed state: one event per transition of the unified order state machine, for every principal, mode and venue
x-spw-webhook-events.payload: { orderId, mode, venue, instrument, status, previous, event, reason, seq, principal, mandateId }
